subject: VPC egress segmentation & service mesh handoff for on-prem k8s
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: ops@groundworks.io, aanand@clientcorp.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: VPC egress segmentation & service mesh handoff for on-prem k8s

Hi Anand / GroundWorks team —

Thanks again for the intake last week. We're drafting the networking handoff so your infra team can stand up the private cluster in your metal racks and meet the client's egress and compliance requirements. I attached an early sketch (RW-ClientCorp-egress-design-v1.pdf) and a quick diagram. Before we lock the design, two constraints from ClientCorp security:

1) All outbound traffic must transit a company-managed egress appliance (no direct internet from nodes).
2) Tenant workloads must be logically segmented so egress rules can be applied per-namespace (billing + compliance).

High-level ask: please confirm whether GroundWorks will provision the egress appliance (HA NAT + TLS inspection) and provide:
- a /29 for the appliance cluster VIPs
- BGP peering detail or static routes to our K8s node subnets
- firewall rules needed for Redwood control-plane callbacks (we'll list ports below)

Notes on our side (preference):
- We plan to use Istio (mTLS) for service-to-service within the cluster and rely on eBPF + Calico egress policies to tag traffic per-namespace before it hits the NAT box.
- For load balancing to external partners, we'll use MetalLB (BGP mode) bound to the node routing plane; if you prefer an external LB, say so.
- Storage: model cache will use local NVMe ephemeral on inference nodes, with Longhorn for persistent configs.

Required ports for Redwood control-plane connectivity (outbound from cluster):
- 443 to api.redwood.com (control plane telemetry & rollout checks)
- 5222/5223 to log collector (if using TCP fallback)

If GroundWorks will not run the appliance, we can supply a hardened VM image and assist with install. Can you confirm the ops owner and preferred timeframe for network acceptance testing?

Thanks — attaching the design and diagram.

— Mina
Mina Haddad
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com

Attachments: RW-ClientCorp-egress-design-v1.pdf (pdf), clientcorp-egress-diagram.png (png)

From: GroundWorks Ops <ops@groundworks.io>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, aanand@clientcorp.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VPC egress segmentation & service mesh handoff for on-prem k8s

Mina, Anand —

Thanks for the clear ask and the diagram. GroundWorks can provision the egress appliance and manage BGP peering. Quick answers inline: 

- Egress appliance: we'll deploy a dual-node HA pair (NAT + TLS inspection) in the aggregation rack. We'll allocate a /29 for VIPs and two public /32s for NAT translation.
- BGP: we support BGP peering with upstream routers. Preferred is using private ASNs; we'll publish routes for the node subnets you provide.
- Firewall: we'll add application-layer allow rules for api.redwood.com and your log collector. Please provide the FQDNs/IPs you need open for the acceptance window.

A few concerns from our SRE team: 
1) MetalLB in BGP mode: if the cluster nodes live behind the egress appliance, we need to ensure the BGP advertisements originate from the node routing plane (we can coordinate with your network team).
2) Per-namespace egress tagging: we can implement uRPF-safe routing but will need the exact label -> CIDR mapping from Redwood so we can write NAT rules per tenant.

Ops owner: Claire Ross <claire.ross@groundworks.io>. ETA for provisioning: 2 weeks once we get node subnet allocations and the NAT VM image if you want us to bake it.

We'll prepare a small runbook for the acceptance test window (BGP session up, synthetic egress checks, control-plane handshake).

— GroundWorks Ops
GroundWorks SRE
ops@groundworks.io

Attachments: none

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, GroundWorks Ops <ops@groundworks.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, aanand@clientcorp.com
Date: Thu, 08 Apr 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VPC egress segmentation & service mesh handoff for on-prem k8s

Thanks — good progress. A few clarifications from Redwood platform/serving runtime side before we finalize: 

1) Egress appliance expectations: if GroundWorks manages the appliance, we need a deterministic NAT mapping table per-namespace (or per-service account) so our telemetry and usage attribution see stable IPs. That means GroundWorks must support static source NAT mapping (not ephemeral SNAT).

2) Service mesh + TLS inspection: Istio mTLS will terminate between pods; any TLS inspection on the appliance must be limited to egress to the public internet. We cannot break intra-cluster mTLS. If packet inspection is required for outbound HTTPS, we prefer an explicit TLS bump policy for only monitored namespaces.

3) MetalLB / BGP: If you prefer MetalLB in BGP mode, advertise the service IP ranges from the node plane. GroundWorks — please confirm whether BGP will be between MetalLB speakers and Spine/Leaf or via a next-hop translation.

4) Storage note (ops): model cache remains local NVMe; ensure that the egress appliance will not NAT local node-to-node traffic (we rely on node internal CIDRs for cache replication). For persistent volumes: Longhorn will use the tenant storage class; we will not require external blockstore egress for regular operations.

Action items: 
- GroundWorks: provide Claire's runbook draft and a sample of the static NAT mapping format (CSV or Netconf).
- Mina/Irene: we'll paste final ports and FQDNs by EOD.
- Marissa: please track procurement of the optional hardened VM image if GroundWorks asks for it.

I'll attach a slightly updated design that converts the rough sketch into a NAT mapping table (RW-ClientCorp-egress-design-v1.pdf updated).

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Platform Engineering — Redwood Inference

Attachments: RW-ClientCorp-egress-design-v1.pdf (updated)

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: VPC egress segmentation & service mesh handoff for on-prem k8s

Folks —

Quick update and next steps after speaking with ClientCorp security: we will proceed with the GroundWorks-managed appliance and the static NAT mapping approach. Summary of what I pushed to Claire:

- NAT mapping format: CSV with columns (namespace, tenant-id, source-cidr, translated-ip). We'll share a sample by COB today.
- Ports/FQDNs: api.redwood.com (443), telemetry.redwood.com (443), logs.collector.clientcorp.net (5223), metrics.push.redwood.com (443).
- Acceptance window: week of Apr 26 (need provisioning complete by Apr 23).

Meeting to kick off network handoff: Tue Apr 13 10:00 PT — Claire and Anand confirmed. I'll send calendar invite and include the runbook template and acceptance checklist from GroundWorks.

Marissa — procurement: please prepare the VM image (hardened Ubuntu 22.04 + iptables config + certs) in case GroundWorks wants us to supply it. If not needed, we'll skip.

Thanks, everyone. Attaching the final diagram and the sample NAT CSV in the Drive link.

— Mina
